Specifically, a review of 5 complaints revealed that your firm did not investigate for software crash incidents in 3 complaints, complaint numbers 0016, 0017, and 0018. Your firm’s procedure QOP-85-02, rev D titled Complaints states in 4.4(b): According to your complaint descriptions, the following events occurred as a result from use of your iMap System, with no formal investigation as to the cause: 1) 0016: The complaint stated, “A crash occurred during the first case after the pre-mapping procedures Clinical Engineer was modifying the geometry by erasing points then paused operations and the iMap software crashed. Team restarted the computer and proceeded with the case... Formal investigation is waived in favor of continued testing, informal investigation by the software team, and continued actions to improve and test stability of the software". 2) 0017: The complaint stated, "Case was completed. Clinical Engineer was modifying the geometry by erasing points. Hill stopped described "heavily" shaving the geometry (erasing and modifying the geometry rendering). When she momentarily stopped erasing the geometry, the iMap software crashed. Team reset the system before the next case but did not continue working on the now-finished case... Formal investigation is waived in favor of continued testing, informal investigation by the software team, and continued actions to improve and test stability of the software per MM-20230310 and MM- 20230809." 3) 0018: The complaint stated, "Team was setting up the iMap system before the case with the patient present. Clinical Engineer opened the iMap software, waited until the localizer screen indicated connection to/proper reading of EM signals via the green lights. Seconds after this occurred, the software crashed. This process was repeated (for a total of two incidents of the same events). Team power cycled the iMap. The iMap program returned to expected operation after this hardware restart. Procedure was able to continue as expected from there." Specifically, A. Your firm's Quality Unit (QU) failed to exercise adequate oversight and did not implement appropriate corrective and preventive actions in response to microbial contamination recovered within the [redacted] ISO 5 containment cell. On 10/25/2025, surface sample [redacted] from [redacted] yielded 1 CFU identified as Serratia marcescens, a gram-negative opportunistic pathogen with known clinical significance. This recovery was documented under deviation UDR 2025-10 and classified as an out-of-trend (OOT) statistical outlier, within established EM alert and action limits. The QU classified this event as major yet assessed the risk as minimal. The QU approved the investigation's conclusion that the probable root cause was "contaminated material introduced during compounding," despite the investigation explicitly noting that these materials were "discarded prior to deviation detection and unavailable for testing." The QU approved the conclusion that the event was a "sporadic environmental contamination" and that "no further corrective actions are required at this time." The QU failed to ensure systemic actions were implemented to prevent recurrence; the only action taken was voluntarily discarding units of Norepinephrine 8mg in 0.9% NaCl 250mL bag Lot [redacted] compounded in [redacted] during the affected production period.
